title: Insert Interval
pattern: One pass: left of it, right of it, or overlapping
statement: `intervals` is a list of non-overlapping intervals **sorted by start**. Insert `newInterval` so that the list stays sorted and non-overlapping, merging wherever necessary.
idea: Carry one **pending** interval (at first the new one) through the sorted list and compare it with each interval.

An interval that ends **before** the pending one starts lies completely to its left: copy it to the result. An interval that **overlaps** the pending one is absorbed: stretch the pending interval to cover both.

The first interval that starts **after** the pending one ends lies completely to its right: the pending interval is finished and goes into the result — and that interval becomes the new pending one. Append whatever is pending at the end.

steps.text: Our example input is drawn on the stage. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
The interval to insert, [4, 8], is the **pending** interval (purple). Walk through the sorted list and compare each interval with it.
[1, 2] ends at 2, **before** the pending interval starts (4). It lies entirely to the left — copy it to the result unchanged.
[3, 5] **overlaps** the pending interval [4, 8]. Absorb it: start = min(4, 3) = 3, end = max(8, 5) = 8. Pending is now **[3, 8]**.
[6, 7] **overlaps** the pending interval [3, 8]. Absorb it: start = min(3, 6) = 3, end = max(8, 7) = 8. Pending is now **[3, 8]**.
[8, 10] **overlaps** the pending interval [3, 8]. Absorb it: start = min(3, 8) = 3, end = max(8, 10) = 10. Pending is now **[3, 10]**.
[12, 16] starts at 12, **after** the pending interval [3, 10] ends. Nothing later can overlap it either, so [3, 10] goes into the result — and [12, 16] becomes the new pending interval.
The list is finished. Whatever is still pending, [12, 16], is appended last.
The new interval has been inserted and merged: **[[1, 2], [3, 10], [12, 16]]**.
Done — the answer is **`[[1,2],[3,10],[12,16]]`**. [4, 8] overlaps [3, 5], [6, 7] and [8, 10]; together they become [3, 10].
